items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: He says, why don't you go see Ike and let him give you some pointers... So I did. I got Ike and I said, Ike, can you come over and help me out... he gave me quite a lift

ctx.x: Well, Ike knows. I know most of the fellows around have them. So, ultimately, we'll get them together for you. You just keep in mind what it is you're after and we'll get them for you. I'll take both of them. Oh, you can dig up stuff, man. You don't know about it. There's one of Ike's that I haven't been able to get yet, but we'll get it one of these days.
Ike, didn't I find your four reasons and bring it to you? Yeah.
Yeah, on the first cut. Frankie Jackson. No, no. That's the late cut you got. Oh, is that so? Yeah, that's the last cut I made. Oh, yes.

items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I tell Nike, he brought a fellow up for me to take a song down.

ctx.x: He knew so much. In the wintertime.

And he had tremendous. And then he was a student of it, too. And he had a fast ear and he picked up stuff that the trumpets would play and he'd slide his fingers on the strings, you know, and to the plane he'd slide it and he'd twist the strings, shove the strings in like you do on the banjo, see. Make a quarter tone, see. Yeah. And we did pretty good until, I don't know, I think the prohibition agents or something happened and they came in and we had to get another job. We went down and made an audition at NBC.…
Would you give up fiddle in this period that you've mentioned? Yes.
